_about: Every eslint-plugin-security finding over the PCA production sources must be fixed or listed here with a reason. check-eslint.mjs fails on any (rule, file) pair that is not listed, or whose count grows. Reviewed 2026-10-09.

eslint-security.reason: Bracket access with a computed key (obj[k]). Warning-level by design: the rule cannot distinguish a validated key from a hostile one. The real risk (prototype pollution via __proto__/constructor/prototype keys) is closed at the source: untrusted JSON enters through the strict parser (own-property __proto__ handling, duplicate-key rejection) and every fuzz target runs a shared-prototype pollution check after each input (Object/Array/Function/String/Number/Uint8Array/Map prototypes, 0 findings across all runs).
Paths are join(dir, fixed file name) under an operator-configured state directory created 0700; no request-derived segment reaches a path.
Command-line tools and test kits that read paths the operator typed on the command line or generated themselves; not reachable from verifier input.
Loads the package's own bundled .wasm from a path derived from __dirname / import.meta.url.
require() over a fixed in-source candidate list (the optional wasm backend by package name, then its sibling dist path); no external input.

Comparisons of public values only: a SHA-256 digest of public receipt data (receipt.ts), JWS header token names (strict-jws.ts) and a private-constructor sentinel object (bls.ts). None involves a secret.

Regex sources that come from signed grants are admitted only after isSafeRegexSource (length caps, no backreferences/lookaround, nested-quantifier ban, 22-bit backtracking budget) and are evaluated against a subject capped at 512 chars; the glob operator no longer uses a RegExp at all. Fuzzed (grammar + mutation + amplification) with a 1 s hang gate: clean.
Validation-time compile of a prohibition pattern that has already passed isSafeRegexSource and the 200-char cap.
Fixed 2026-10-09: now guarded by isSafeRegexSource, a 200-char pattern cap and the 512-char subject cap before compilation.
Interpolates a field name from a fixed in-source list (tcbInfo / qeIdentity), never input text.
Interpolates the chip family named by the signature-verified GPU report; escaped 2026-10-09 so no report byte can change the pattern.

Heuristic star-height flag. Each pattern was measured with 200k-character adversarial inputs (digit runs, dotted runs, quote and escape runs, whitespace runs): all finish in under 3 ms (anchored, unambiguous alternation, or bounded repeats). The scanner-style patterns that DID blow up (Rego allow rule, Cedar word-operator and scope clauses) were fixed, not suppressed.
Remaining numeric-literal pattern ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$ (linear) and the allow-rule pattern, which was quadratic and is fixed (one whitespace gap per position; regression test with 200k spaces).
Not a security finding: the file carries eslint-disable comments for a rule this security-only config does not load (reported as an unknown rule).
Same artefact: an eslint-disable comment for no-control-regex, which this security-only config does not load.

Anchored, unambiguous patterns measured linear on 200k-character inputs; the scope-clause and word-operator patterns that were quadratic (adjacent whitespace gaps, lazy group before \s+) were rewritten and carry regression tests.

gitleaks: tools/pca-audit/static/gitleaks.toml carries its own reasoned allowlist (194 raw hits, all published test vectors, public attestation captures or build output).

osv-pnpm.reason: 0.8.10 -> 0.8.15 in packages/pca (15 advisories; parses NVIDIA RIM XML before the signature is verified).

Transitive of the optional snarkjs/circom toolchain (zero-knowledge path). The advisories are DoS on attacker-controlled glob / deep-object input; PCA passes neither (no globbing of untrusted text; no untrusted objects into underscore). Fix by upgrading snarkjs when its range allows.
Pulled only through pca-ai-sdk (the Vercel AI SDK peer chain). HTTP-client/multipart advisories in code the PCA adapter never calls; the integrator's own AI SDK version governs.
Pulled only through pca-langchain's LangChain peer chain; not used by the PCA guard.
Dev/peer dependency of the pca-fastify, pca-mcp and pca-llamaindex adapters; the integrator supplies and patches their own framework.
pca-next adapter's framework peer chain; the integrator's Next.js version governs.

osv-cargo.reason: No patched release exists (crate is unmaintained). 0290 is AVX2-only and the crate is built for wasm32 (no AVX2). KyberSlash (variable-time division in compress/message encoding) is a real timing weakness of this K-PKE; the lattice base-OT is an experimental research construction and is documented as not side-channel hardened. Replacing the K-PKE with a constant-time implementation is a follow-up.
Unmaintained-crate notices (no vulnerability) in the folding / stark / zkVM proof crates' dependency trees.
Present only in the zkVM host dependency tree via the prover SDK; PCA performs no RSA operation.
Transitive of the zkVM toolchain; PCA verifiers do not log untrusted input through it.

clippy.reason: Library and binary targets are clippy -D warnings clean; the remaining lints (needless_range_loop, doc_overindented_list_items) are style lints in adversarial test code that indexes parallel arrays on purpose.
Two style lints (doc_lazy_continuation, manual_is_multiple_of) in a crate under active development by another workstream; not security relevant.
